_note: Indonesia wiring round (post-triage full sweep of the 74 measured orphans, per project memory triage_2026-08-30 and unlinked_nodes_cleared). Method: 6 parallel research subagents (one per theme: trade/ports, energy/mining/climate, agriculture/fisheries/environment, population/social/health, fiscal/finance/governance, regional/local/digital), each independently fetching primary sources and reporting structured findings (not writing files). Every proposed edge and every new-node citation was then independently re-fetched and verified by the orchestrating session before minting -- including, for the two BPS Cloudflare-walled PDFs backing the largest edge clusters (Energy Balances of Indonesia; the GHG/Energy-Flow Accounts), by opening the BPS page in a real browser (Claude in Chrome), reading the signed web-api.bps.go.id download link out of the DOM, and curling the PDF directly with a Referer header -- confirming every quote verbatim on the actual extracted PDF text, not the landing-page abstract. No fabricated or unverifiable quote survived into this file. id-energy-balance-detail was deliberately left unwired and flagged instead as a likely duplicate of id-energy-balances (see _dropped) rather than minting the same evidence onto both nodes. Two containment relationships (id-export-partners, id-commodity-partner-matrix as part_of id-foreign-trade-exports) were recorded as a part_of field patch to the existing id-indonesia-grok-2026-08.json seed file, not as edges here -- per project convention, part_of does not reduce the isolated-node count.

reports.publisher: Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM)
reports.description: Indonesia's national ministry for energy and mineral resources. Named as a source institution (generically, not by a specific document title) in BPS's Energy Balance of Indonesia ("Sumber data ... berasal dari berbagai publikasi yang diterbitkan oleh ... Kementerian Energi dan Sumber Daya Mineral") and its GHG Emissions Accounts ("Statistik Energi dari Kementerian Energi dan Sumber Daya Mineral (ESDM)"). reports.title: Statistics PLN
reports.description: PT PLN's own annual statistical report on generation capacity, generation mix, sales and distribution. Cited by exact title in BPS's Electricity Statistics 2020-2024 bibliography: "PT PLN (Persero). 2025. Statistics PLN 2024."

reports.title: PT Perusahaan Gas Negara (PGN) Tbk
reports.description: Indonesia's state-owned natural gas transmission and distribution company. Named (generically, not by a specific document title) as one of the institutional data sources for BPS's Energy Balance of Indonesia.

reports.title: BPH Migas (Badan Pengatur Hilir Minyak dan Gas Bumi)
reports.description: Indonesia's downstream oil and gas regulatory agency. Named (generically, not by a specific document title) as one of the institutional data sources for BPS's Energy Balance of Indonesia.

reports.title: PT Kereta Api Indonesia (KAI) (Persero)
reports.description: Indonesia's state railway operator. Named (generically, not by a specific document title) as one of the institutional data sources — rail fuel consumption — for BPS's Energy Balance of Indonesia.

reports.title: Direktorat Jenderal Minyak dan Gas Bumi (Ditjen Migas)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM)
reports.description: ESDM's Directorate General of Oil and Gas. Its own oil and gas production statistics are cited as a chart-level source ("Sumber/Source: Dirjen Migas ESDM 2023") in BPS's Mining Statistics of Petroleum and Natural Gas 2019-2023, alongside BPS's own primary Annual Survey of Petroleum and Natural Gas Mining Companies.

reports.title: National GHG Inventory Report and MRV (SIGN SMART)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Environment and Forestry (KLHK), Directorate General of Climate Change Control
reports.description: Indonesia's official national greenhouse gas inventory and Monitoring-Reporting-Verification report (e.g. "Laporan Inventarisasi Gas Rumah Kaca (GRK) dan Monitoring, Pelaporan, Verifikasi (MPV) 2023"), maintained via the SIGN SMART platform. Cited as a named source in BPS's GHG Emissions Accounts and referenced (as "National GHGs Inventory System (SIGNSMART)") in Indonesia's Second NDC.

reports.title: Population Administration Information System (SIAK) — Dukcapil Civil Registry Data
reports.publisher: Directorate General of Population and Civil Registration (Ditjen Dukcapil), Ministry of Home Affairs
reports.description: National civil-registration/vital-statistics administrative database (Sistem Informasi Administrasi Kependudukan) maintained by Ditjen Dukcapil, Kemendagri. Its semester population counts, including religion breakdowns, are distributed via the Satu Data Indonesia portal (Kementerian Agama dataset listing "Sumber Data: Dukcapil") and used to reconcile BPS/Kemensos's DTSEN social registry.

reports.title: Data Tunggal Sosial Ekonomi Nasional (DTSEN)
reports.publisher: BPS – Statistics Indonesia (jointly with Ministry of Social Affairs)
reports.description: Single integrated individual/household socio-economic registry built and quarterly updated by BPS — combining Susenas, Sakernas, administrative data and reconciled with Dukcapil population records — that since 2025 serves as the unified targeting basis for Indonesia's social-protection programmes (PKH, Sembako food assistance, JKN/BPJS Kesehatan subsidies, Sekolah Rakyat, housing assistance), replacing the earlier DTKS system.

_dropped.why: RESOLVED 2026-08-30 (Thomas ruling): confirmed duplicate, merge into id-energy-balances. Node `id-energy-balance-detail` removed from the corpus. Flagging for Thomas's ruling, not asserting as resolved: 2026-08-30 research could not find any BPS publication distinctly titled/scoped as a 'detailed production-consumption' energy balance separate from 'Neraca Energi Indonesia' (which is what id-energy-balances' new edges this round cite). The two nodes' own descriptions ('Annual energy balance covering production, conversion and consumption' vs 'covering production through final consumption... extends the earlier Energy Balances node with fuller multi-year detail') read as the same underlying BPS product described twice from the 2026-08-14 Indonesia Grok batch import. Left id-energy-balance-detail unwired this round rather than duplicate the same edges onto both nodes without a document distinguishing them — a genuine duplicate-node merge call, not a research gap.

BPS provincial/kota statistics-table pages (Sultra, Kendari, Kolaka) for inter-island trade volume returned landing-page metadata only, no source/methodology text. A BPS Belitung training-news article suggested inter-island trade data collection may be organisationally bundled with the interprovincial-trade (PAW) survey, but did not explicitly state a derivation/containment relationship — too ambiguous to assert.

KEK.go.id/BPS coordination-meeting articles describe an intent to integrate KEK statistics ahead of the 2026 Economic Census but name no existing BPS/BKPM product as a current data source. BKPM's LKPM dataset lists KEK names only as a form dropdown, not a structured linkage.

jdih.kemenkeu.go.id's KPBPB legal glossary names no data-source agency. A BPS Batam 'Import Statistics of Batam' publication sources from Batam Customs forms (PIB-BC 2.0 / PPBI-BC 2.3), a customs-forms-level detail about a non-cataloged BPS sub-product, not a documented statement that id-ftz itself derives from id-customs-tariff.

BPS 'Statistik Transportasi Laut' publication abstracts state only that data is 'bersourced from Indonesian seaports generally', naming no institution. SIRUSA metadata (kd=2168) 500-errored/robots-disallowed on every attempt.

BPS 'Statistik Transportasi Provinsi DKI Jakarta 2024' abstract names real institutional data providers (Dinas Perhubungan DKI Jakarta, Ditlantas Polda Metro Jaya, PT Transportasi Jakarta, PT KAI, PT Pelindo, PT Angkasa Pura II) but none of these institutions are cataloged report-nodes in the graph. A real lead if/when institution-level transport nodes are minted.

BPS publishes genuine Tanjung Priok-specific statistics tables, but every fetch returned landing/navigation chrome only, no footnote/source line. A Databoks secondary article citing 'BPS' sourced itself to 'Katadata Insight Center', not a specific BPS publication.
Same class of BPS statistics-table landing pages as Tanjung Priok — body text unretrievable on every attempt.

BPS runs city-level port-transport editions (e.g. 'Statistik Transportasi Laut Kota Makassar 2024') analogous in structure to id-cpi/id-cpi-provincial, but no document states a dependency relationship between the city editions and this national node — a title-pattern similarity only, not a citation.

Kemenkeu's 'Nota Keuangan RAPBN TA 2024' PDF is the right primary-document type (state-budget financial note allocating spending per ministry including Kemhan) but only front-matter/table-of-contents was retrieved, not the Belanja Negara chapter itself — needs a follow-up fetch targeting later PDF pages, not a dead end.

BPS's 'Statistik Pertambangan Non Minyak dan Gas Bumi 2019-2023' states its own data is from BPS's Survei Perusahaan Pertambangan Non Migas (a primary BPS survey). Its foreword names Ditjen Minerba/ESDM only as general cooperation/access-facilitation language, not as a specific cited data source — too weak to assert an edge.
Same publication and same reasoning as id-nickel above — BPS primary-collection product, ESDM cooperation language only.
'Statistik Pertambangan Bahan Galian Indonesia 2023' (quarrying) states its data is from BPS's own Survei Tahunan Perusahaan Penggalian — a primary BPS survey, no named external dependency.

All land-cover/land-use-change data found (KLHK/BPS Statistik Lingkungan Hidup, FRL, BUR3) is attributed generically to 'MoEF/KLHK land cover' and matches the id-forest-cover node rather than a distinct land-use-change publication tied to agriculture/estates.

KSA (Kerangka Sampel Area) survey methodology is a BPS+BPPT/LAPAN+ATR/BPN+BIG collaboration, but none of those agencies are corpus nodes, and no document states id-national-accounts/id-poverty/id-agriculture-stats are calculated specifically from this publication rather than raw BPS crop data generally.
Ministry of Agriculture's 'Buku Statistik Pertanian 2023' preface names BPS/BKPM/BMKG as general 'data producers' without a specific citable sentence tying it to an existing/new corpus node.

BPS 'Statistik Kelapa Sawit Indonesia 2023' sources from its own Plantation Estate Survey, Ministry of Agriculture's Ditjenbun (not a corpus node) for smallholder data, and 'custom documents from Directorate General of Customs' for trade figures — the trade sentence does not name id-foreign-trade-exports/imports specifically.

BPS 'Statistik Air Bersih' methodology (via a neliti.com mirror) states it is BPS's own Annual Survey of Water Supply Establishments, with its sampling frame drawn from the 2006 Economic Census — not a node in this graph.

BPS's VIMK (quarterly micro/small industry survey) sampling method is confirmed as two-stage PPS selection of Census Blocks from updated household listings — explicitly not drawn from the Manufacturing Industry Directory (which the directory's own abstract scopes to medium/large firms only).

BPS PPI abstracts/press releases state only 'dilaksanakan oleh Badan Pusat Statistik' (BPS-conducts-BPS-survey), not a dependency on another node. SIRUSA metadata pages for PPI persistently 500-errored/ROBOTS_DISALLOWED.

Two independently-hosted mirrors of 'Provinsi DKI Jakarta Dalam Angka' PDFs were found; the 2011 edition gives only generic sourcing language, and the 2022 edition's PDF returned only its table of contents on repeated fetches — no chapter-level sourcing sentence retrieved.
BPS Jabar abstract pages give no methodology detail; the one full-PDF mirror found (bappelitbangda.purwakartakab.go.id) 502'd/robots-blocked on every attempt.
A 'Jawa Tengah Dalam Angka 2025' PDF was located (owncloud.jatengprov.go.id via bappeda.jatengprov.go.id) but is robots-disallowed to WebFetch; no alternate accessible copy found.
No non-BPS-hosted full-text 'Jawa Timur Dalam Angka' PDF was located; BPS Jatim publication pages returned abstracts only, same pattern as the other provinces.

A 2011 'Kota Magelang Dalam Angka' PDF loaded but only returned body text through Chapter III (Population); later economy/PDRB chapters were not retrievable across repeated fetches. The only concrete sourcing found was a local civil-registry table footnote, not a BPS national-survey citation. No containment language found either (reads as a standalone publication, like Malang).

This node is a generic/categorical placeholder for the Dalam Angka publication pattern, which this round evidenced concretely via a specific city (id-malang). No additional document specific to this generic node (as opposed to one particular city) was found or expected.

BPS press releases on the 2025 IKN special population enumeration (Pendataan Penduduk IKN) explicitly frame it as novel and standalone ('wilayah IKN belum pernah tercatat secara khusus dalam sensus penduduk sebelumnya') rather than derived from the existing Population Census. Results-announcement article does not name Podes, PDRB or RPJMN as sources it draws on (checked and confirmed absent).

BPS 'Statistik Wisatawan Nusantara 2024' describes its own sources as Mobile Positioning Data (telco big-data) and a standalone 'Survei Digital Wisatawan Nusantara 2024' web-questionnaire — not Susenas-derived. No document ties its sampling frame to Susenas, Podes or the Population Census.

SIRUSA metadata (kegiatan/50171) confirms the 'Statistik Objek Daya Tarik Wisata' collection unit is a standalone business/establishment survey ('Usaha/perusahaan'), not one drawing on Podes as hypothesized.

BPS 'Statistik E-Commerce 2023' abstract has topic-coverage language only. Every attempt to reach the full PDF failed (web-api.bps.go.id 403 on two URLs, a dataindonesia.id mirror 403'd, a Scribd copy rendered a JS-disabled error shell, AllStats Search returned zero indexed results).
